Summary
Data source overview:  
The paper examines limitations in existing formal verification methods for autonomous cyber-physical systems (CPS) and proposes the FOSSIL family of approaches that combine symbolic safety monitoring with end-to-end reinforcement learning, perceptual template matching, and online program synthesis to maintain formal guarantees despite perception uncertainty and model mismatch.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[87]

Inference strategy justification:  
Most causal links and interventions are explicitly discussed. Moderate inference (confidence 2) was applied only when connecting well-motivated but future-work ideas (e.g. temporal-invariant vision verification) to the central risk fabric.

Extraction completeness explanation:  
All three top-level limitations called out in the Introduction plus the statistical-evidence bottleneck are represented. Every methodological step (template matching, runtime monitors, program-synthesis adaptation) and every actionable research direction (temporal vision verification, runtime assumption monitors) appears as an intervention node, with intermediate concept nodes preserving the argument flow. Every node participates in at least one path from the core risk to at least one intervention, forming a single connected fabric.

Key limitations:  
• The source is a position/vision paper; quantitative evidence strengths had to be rated “medium” (3) in most cases.  
• Implementation detail in the paper is high-level; lifecycle placement and maturity assessments necessarily rely on judgement.  
• Some auxiliary claims (e.g. specific hybrid-logic syntax) were omitted because they do not alter causal-interventional structure.

Potential instruction-set improvement:  
Clarify whether “addressed_by” versus “mitigated_by” should be preferred for challenge→approach edges and supply a small example. Provide an explicit rule for representing multiple parallel interventions that share the same preceding concept node to avoid naming divergence, and allow optional grouping of structurally identical confidence rationales to reduce verbosity.
